body.title: w13n-no-answer-go: an unanswered write may be stored, and dsh's body is an object
body.summary: Two changes to office_request. An unanswered write now says it may or may not be stored and names reading it back; a read keeps the plain sentence. The body is declared a JSON object with any keys in the one shared definition. Four commits, all proofs green.

blocks.heading: What was asked and what was done
blocks.text:
Piece 1, from argus's message eILVKeOHc0ts: when fetch throws, askTheOffice (tools/office-request.mjs) names the reason for every method. A write now gets: "The office did not answer (<why>), so this write may or may not be stored. Read it back through office_request before you send it again; never send it another way." A GET keeps "The office did not answer (<why>)." Keys stay replaced in both, and the tool never sends the write again itself. A comment names eILVKeOHc0ts.

Piece 2: officeRequestDefinition's body is now { type: 'object', additionalProperties: true, description: 'The JSON body, for POST, PUT and PATCH.' } — the one place the fact lives. tools/office-mcp.mjs no longer translates 'json' to 'object'; the type comes straight from the definition. dsh compiles that shape to a real object type and refuses a string body itself (seen by hand on dsh 0.1.5-rc.2, 17 Oct 2026; not tested here).
